title: Emberfall
logline: The last Cinderwarden rides across a blighted continent to unmake a king's crown, and every road she takes decides who the realm will become.

plot.premise: The Fall began when the Crown of Embers slipped its lock. Husks of ember and ash walk the roads. Sael Ironbrook, last of the Cinderwardens and exiled for a killing she could not avoid, must choose between a Regent who wants the Crown as a weapon, an Order that would burn the infected with the cure, and an old archivist who believes the Crown can be unmade. Three seals, one king, and the question of what a warden is for.

characters.name: Sael Ironbrook
characters.role: player; last of the Cinderwardens, exiled
characters.bio: Trained to hunt what the blight makes. Exiled after striking down a corrupted fellow warden.

characters.name: Brother Cael
characters.role: prior of the Order of Ash

characters.name: Auric Vael, the Cinder King
characters.role: final boss; the king who wore the Crown of Embers

acts.title: Ashes at the Vale
acts.summary: Sael limps into Hearth Vale as husks pour out of the night. Defend the village, recover the warden cache, win a horse, and follow Lioren's letter.

do.text: Warden Signs unlocked: Aard-like push, Fire sign and Ward.
Whistle for Ash with the call key.
Contracts are posted on notice boards. Each pays crowns and teaches a creature.

acts.title: The Roads to Gildmere
acts.summary: The Mirewood, the trade city and its politics. The Regent wants a weapon; the archivist knows the Crown is a lock.

acts.title: The Fractured Alliance
acts.summary: Saltmarch burns or does not. Lioren stands or falls. Three seals wait on the Stonecrown, in the Barrens and in Frostreach.

acts.title: The Crown of Embers
acts.summary: Ride to the Veil. The king waits; the Crown listens. Cure, seize, deliver or burn.

gates.hint: The Gildguard want a writ or a good word.
The ledge is beyond a gap only a glider can cross.
The Barrens burn the unprepared. Firebane or Ember Plate.
Warm cloaks and hot food will keep Frostreach from freezing you.
Three seal stones open the Veil.
Only a warden's ring opens the cache.
The Gildmere archive holds the key to the Barrow.

n1.say: Warden! Gods, you are a sight. Husks in the east field. Three villagers cut, and I have no salve left.

n2.say: Then take the east gate. Try to leave the barn standing.

n3.say: Husks. They were people. Something under the mountain wakes them with ember. You would know better than I.

n1.say: You are not sleeping, Sael. Sit. Let me see that cinder-burn.

n2.say: Herbs and ember dust, stirred anticlockwise. Be careful, it poisons if you drink too many.

n3.say: Herbs, ember dust, a patient hand.

n4.say: Rest when you can. Not like you will.

n1.say: Your blade, warden. I cleaned it when you were out cold. Silver does not forget, but it needs oil.

n2.say: Repairs are free for a warden. Hold still. There.

n3.say: Four ore and a bit of hide. Steel will do till you can afford better.

n4.say: Under the forge. Wardens kept a cache there before the fall. You will want the ring. I left it where I found it.

n1.say: The grey mare was your warden-master's. She has not let a soul ride since he died. Maybe she will let you.

n2.say: Hold the bridle low. Do not look her in the eye until she looks at you.

n3.say: Not on the Mirewood roads. Come back when you change your mind.

n1.say: She trusts you. That is rarer than a clean boot in the Mirewood. Take care of her.
You're the warden! I have a letter from Lioren. He said to give it only to Sael or to no one.

choices.text: Why did he leave it with a child?

n2.say: He went to Saltmarch. He said you would understand why. He said the Order was lying.

n3.say: Nobody looks at me. I am good at keeping things.

n1.say: When I grow up, I will carry a light like that for everybody.
Sael. They told me you were dead. They told me a great many things.

n2.say: The Order is burning the quarantine district. Cael says it is mercy. I say it is the first step to burning everything with a pulse.

choices.text: You left me to take the blame.

n3.say: Always. My blade is yours until the Crown breaks.

n4.say: I know. I have said sorry in my head a thousand times. Hear it aloud: sorry.

n5.say: Then I follow no one. Find me when you have decided what kind of warden you are.

n1.say: Quiet night. Too quiet. Do you remember the vows?

n2.say: Hunt what hunts the helpless. And spare what can be spared. Gods, you still have it.

n3.say: Then I will say them for both of us.

n1.say: A warden in my fog. I expected nothing so shiny. What do you want, silver-edge?

choices.text: Antidote for the cinder-touch. A friend is dying.
I hear you brew potions the Gilds cannot.
There is a hag in your fog.

n2.say: Cinder-touch. A rotten way to go. Two bog lilies and a pinch of cinder salt, and I will teach you the stir. Free, because I loathe the Order.

n3.say: I trade in knowledge. Bring me a hag's eye, I teach you a hard recipe.

n4.say: Old Gretch. She was my teacher. Do not kill her unless you must. If you must, take the eye and give it to me.

n1.say: The last Cinderwarden, in my hall. I am told you once refused a king's writ. Refuse mine and you will find Gildmere less forgiving.

n2.say: Here is my offer. The blight rises from the Crown of Embers beneath Mount Karth. Bring it to me, and I will build lances that burn the husks from the roads. Gildmere will feed and arm you.

choices.text: You want a weapon. The Crown is no weapon.

n3.say: Everything is a weapon, warden. The only question is whose.

n4.say: I have. Four patrols, none returned. The Crown reaches into men.

n5.say: Consider quickly. My patience has a short fuse.

n6.say: Wise. Captain Halvard will give you a writ to pass the guard lines. And Archivist Neris will tell you what the Crown cost the last king.

n1.say: Well? Do you have what I asked for?

choices.text: The seals are mine. Soon the Crown.

n3.say: Then the realm is nearly saved. Do not make me regret the trust.

n1.say: State your business, warden. Make it short; the Regent has doubled the patrols since Saltmarch.

choices.text: I need a writ to pass your lines.

n2.say: The Order locked the quarantine gate. Cael says to burn it. Seren's ferry still runs; half the district has fled by water.

n3.say: Seal-stamped. Go with the shield, not the sword. Your road is the south gate.

n4.say: I trust my men. The Regent signs my pay and my orders; I will do the one and weigh the other.

n1.say: A warden in the archive. You have no idea how long it has been since a warden asked a question I could answer.

n2.say: The Crown of Embers is not a weapon. It is a lock. A king wore it to hold the cinder under Karth in sleep. When he died, the lock slipped.

n3.say: A good king. He refused a hundred offers to use the Crown for war. He is still wearing it, I think, in a way.

n4.say: Three scrolls. Then you can break the lock rather than carry it. Three seal stones; the Stonecrown, the Barrens, Frostreach. Each guarded by what the king left behind.

n1.say: The last warden. You carry the sin of the Fall. But I do not hate you; hate is a fire that burns the holder.

n2.say: The blight spreads by contact. Every infected village I burn saves ten. This is not cruelty, it is arithmetic.

choices.text: Open the quarantine gate. Let them leave by water.
There is another way. Give me three days.

n3.say: Then the fire will find the water. You will answer for every husk that rises from your mercy.

n4.say: Blessed be the hand that does hard work.

n5.say: Three days. Not one more. The Order can wait; the flame cannot.

n1.say: The Order's accounts remember. When the blight asks for a ledger, I will present yours.
You are the warden who opened the gate. Half of Saltmarch is on my boat and the other half is praying. I owe you more than I can pay.

choices.text: Take them to Gildmere. Tell Halvard I sent you.
Tell me about the coast road.

n2.say: The captain will not welcome refugees. But I will make him.

n3.say: Bad weather, worse roads. If you ever need a boat, I know the shallows to the Barrens.

n1.say: Little warden climb tall rock? Orsk show. Orsk good at rock. Orsk hate Crown, Crown make rock angry.

choices.text: Teach me to climb the Stonecrown.
How do I kill the stone giant?

n2.say: Orsk give cloth. Cloth catch wind, you fall slow. Rest on ledge, not on rock that moves.

n3.say: Glowing eye in his back. Hit eye, he fall. Hit knee first.

n4.say: Orsk. Mountain is mother. Mountain sick now.

n1.say: I know your oath-words, warden. I wrote them.

n2.say: The Crown holds a hunger that outlasts kings. It chose me, and I was too proud to refuse. Now it wears me.

choices.text: The seals are set. I can unmake the Crown.
Give me the Crown. I will carry it.
The Order will purify this land of you.

n_cure.say: Do it. Do it before I remember what I want.

n_throne.say: You would rule the ember? Be the lock I could not be. Then take it from me.

n_dominion.say: Another small king wanting a large crown. Come and take it.

n_purify.say: Burn me and the hills and the fields. I will be a mercy to no one.

entries.title: Cinder Husks
entries.text: People or beasts burned hollow by the blight. They crave warmth and take it.

entries.title: The Cinderwardens
entries.text: An order of hunters that kept the blight to a handful of villages. Sael is the last.

entries.title: The Order of Ash
entries.text: A faith that believes the blight must be burned out, with whatever it clings to.

entries.title: Lioren Vask
entries.text: Sael's rival and friend. Left a letter before disappearing to Saltmarch.

entries.title: The Mirewood
entries.text: A drowned forest where fog hides everything, including dangers older than the Fall.

entries.title: Cinder-touch
entries.text: A slow curse. The skin cracks with ember; the victim hungers. A cure exists, with the right salt.

entries.title: The Regent's Offer
entries.text: Tavian wants the Crown as a weapon. Halvard distrusts the order but obeys.

entries.title: The Crown's Reach
entries.text: Four patrols entered the Barrow, none returned.

entries.title: The Crown Is a Lock
entries.text: King Auric wore the Crown to hold the cinder beneath Karth asleep.

entries.title: Auric Vael
entries.text: A king who refused a hundred offers to arm the Crown.

entries.title: The Hollow Barrow
entries.text: A crypt of the old court. Wights guard Auric's scrolls.

entries.title: The Three Seals
entries.text: Seal stones on the Stonecrown, in the Barrens and in Frostreach. Together they unmake the lock.

entries.title: The Saltmarch Fire
entries.text: The Order burned a quarantine of two hundred souls. The Gildmere refugees say the smoke stood for three days.

entries.title: Lioren's Fever
entries.text: Lioren has cinder-touch. He hid it from everyone, including himself.

entries.title: The Stonecrown
entries.text: The mountain range where crag-kin still live. Some peaks are the sleeping Titans.

entries.title: The Crag Titan
entries.text: A stone giant grown over with ember crystals. The eye in its back glows.

entries.title: The Crown Spire
entries.text: A tower built to hold a king who would not die.

entries.title: Cinder Stag
entries.text: Cursed deer whose antlers burn. Their antlers are useful for ember-forging.

entries.title: Marsh Hag
entries.text: An alchemist who stayed in the Mirewood too long.

say.text: You are alive. Do not move. Do not speak.

fx.text: Gildmere, jewel of the trade roads

say.text: Tell Wren I remembered the vow.

barks.say: A hammer rings from the smithy.
Something splashes in the black water.
The ground ticks like a cooling forge.
Keep your blade sheathed inside the walls, warden.
I hate the fog. It never forgets a footstep.
Hold lock-on to face a single enemy; dodge to avoid strong attacks.
Fresh bread, warm from the oven!

endings.title: The Lock Unmade
endings.epilogue: Sael sets the three seal stones around the Crown and speaks the unmaking. The cinder under Karth sleeps. Auric, free of the Crown, closes his eyes. Husks fall to ash that is only ash. Saltmarch remembers; Gildmere argues; the Order scatters. Lioren, if he lives, tends a vale-side forge with Edda. Wren carries a lantern at night.

endings.title: The Ember Throne
endings.epilogue: Sael takes up the Crown. The cinder obeys. The blight recedes into the mountain, and so does Sael: a warden no one visits, in a hall no one finds. Ash waits at the Veil's edge for a rider who does not come.

endings.title: A Realm of Lances
endings.epilogue: The Crown goes to Gildmere. Tavian's lances burn the husks from the roads, then the roads the husks came from, then the villages that disagreed. Halvard resigns. Neris keeps the true account where no one can find it.

endings.title: Purifying Fire
endings.epilogue: The Order sweeps the Veil with fire. The cinder dies in the burning and the burning keeps going. Cael writes a long ledger of the cost; Sael carries it north, alone.

endings.title: Hollow Victory
endings.epilogue: The king falls and the Crown rolls from his brow, still hot. No one has decided what to do with it. The blight grows quiet and then restless, waiting for the next to wear it.
